paragraphs.text: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, hath found according to the flesh?
paragraphs.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;
paragraphs.translit: Ti oun eroumen heurēkenai Abraam ton propatora hēmōn kata sarka;

paragraphs.text: For if Abraham was justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not toward God.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλʼ οὐ πρὸς θεόν,
paragraphs.translit: ei gar Abraam ex ergōn edikaiōthē, echei kauchēma· allʼ ou pros theon,

paragraphs.text: For what saith the scripture? And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness.
paragraphs.original: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
paragraphs.translit: ti gar hē graphē legei; Episteusen de Abraam tō theō kai elogisthē autō eis dikaiosynēn.

paragraphs.text: Now to him that worketh, the reward is not reckoned as of grace, but as of debt.
paragraphs.original: τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·
paragraphs.translit: tō de ergazomenō ho misthos ou logizetai kata charin alla kata opheilēma·

paragraphs.text: But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is reckoned for righteousness.
paragraphs.original: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην,
paragraphs.translit: tō de mē ergazomenō, pisteuonti de epi ton dikaiounta ton asebē, logizetai hē pistis autou eis dikaiosynēn,

paragraphs.text: Even as David also pronounceth blessing upon the man, unto whom God reckoneth righteousness apart from works,
paragraphs.original: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων·
paragraphs.translit: kathaper kai Dauid legei ton makarismon tou anthrōpou hō ho theos logizetai dikaiosynēn chōris ergōn·

paragraphs.text: [saying], Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, And whose sins are covered.
paragraphs.original: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι,
paragraphs.translit: Makarioi hōn aphethēsan hai anomiai kai hōn epekalyphthēsan hai hamartiai,

paragraphs.text: Blessed is the man to whom, the Lord will not reckon sin.
paragraphs.original: μακάριος ἀνὴρ οὗ οὐ μὴ λογίσηται κύριος ἁμαρτίαν.
paragraphs.translit: makarios anēr hou ou mē logisētai kyrios hamartian.

paragraphs.text: Is this blessing then pronounced upon the circumcision, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say, To Abraham his faith was reckoned for righteousness.
paragraphs.original: Ὁ μακαρισμὸς οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν περιτομὴν ἢ καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκροβυστίαν; λέγομεν γάρ· Ἐλογίσθη τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἡ πίστις εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
paragraphs.translit: Ho makarismos oun houtos epi tēn peritomēn ē kai epi tēn akrobystian; legomen gar· Elogisthē tō Abraam hē pistis eis dikaiosynēn.

paragraphs.text: How then was it reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision:
paragraphs.original: πῶς οὖν ἐλογίσθη; ἐν περιτομῇ ὄντι ἢ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ; οὐκ ἐν περιτομῇ ἀλλʼ ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ·
paragraphs.translit: pōs oun elogisthē; en peritomē onti ē en akrobystia; ouk en peritomē allʼ en akrobystia·

paragraphs.text: and he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had while he was in uncircumcision; that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might be reckoned unto them;
paragraphs.original: καὶ σημεῖον ἔλαβεν περιτομῆς, σφραγῖδα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐν τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πατέρα πάντων τῶν πιστευόντων διʼ ἀκροβυστίας, εἰς τὸ λογισθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὴν δικαιοσύνην,
paragraphs.translit: kai sēmeion elaben peritomēs, sphragida tēs dikaiosynēs tēs pisteōs tēs en tē akrobystia, eis to einai auton patera pantōn tōn pisteuontōn diʼ akrobystias, eis to logisthēnai autois tēn dikaiosynēn,

paragraphs.text: and the father of circumcision to them who not only are of the circumcision, but who also walk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham which he had in uncircumcision.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πατέρα περιτομῆς τοῖς οὐκ ἐκ περιτομῆς μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς στοιχοῦσιν τοῖς ἴχνεσιν τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἀβραάμ.
paragraphs.translit: kai patera peritomēs tois ouk ek peritomēs monon alla kai tois stoichousin tois ichnesin tēs en akrobystia pisteōs tou patros hēmōn Abraam.

paragraphs.text: For not through the law was the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he should be heir of the world, but through the righteousness of faith.
paragraphs.original: Οὐ γὰρ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία τῷ Ἀβραὰμ ἢ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ, τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ δικαιοσύνης πίστεως·
paragraphs.translit: Ou gar dia nomou hē epangelia tō Abraam ē tō spermati autou, to klēronomon auton einai kosmou, alla dia dikaiosynēs pisteōs·

paragraphs.text: For if they that are of the law are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of none effect:
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία·
paragraphs.translit: ei gar hoi ek nomou klēronomoi, kekenōtai hē pistis kai katērgētai hē epangelia·

paragraphs.text: for the law worketh wrath; but where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ νόμος ὀργὴν κατεργάζεται, οὗ δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νόμος, οὐδὲ παράβασις.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar nomos orgēn katergazetai, hou de ouk estin nomos, oude parabasis.

paragraphs.text: For this cause [it is] of faith, that [it may be] according to grace; to the end that the promise may be sure to all the seed; not to that only which is of the law, but to that also which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all
paragraphs.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ πίστεως, ἵνα κατὰ χάριν, εἰς τὸ εἶναι βεβαίαν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν παντὶ τῷ σπέρματι, οὐ τῷ ἐκ τοῦ νόμου μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἐκ πίστεως Ἀβραάμ (ὅς ἐστιν πατὴρ πάντων ἡμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Dia touto ek pisteōs, hina kata charin, eis to einai bebaian tēn epangelian panti tō spermati, ou tō ek tou nomou monon alla kai tō ek pisteōs Abraam (hos estin patēr pantōn hēmōn,

paragraphs.text: (as it is written, A father of many nations have I made thee) before him whom he believed, [even] God, who giveth life to the dead, and calleth the things that are not, as though they were.
paragraphs.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα·
paragraphs.translit: kathōs gegraptai hoti Patera pollōn ethnōn tetheika se), katenanti hou episteusen theou tou zōopoiountos tous nekrous kai kalountos ta mē onta hōs onta·

paragraphs.text: Who in hope believed against hope, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, So shall thy seed be.
paragraphs.original: ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου·
paragraphs.translit: hos parʼ elpida epʼ elpidi episteusen eis to genesthai auton patera pollōn ethnōn kata to eirēmenon· Houtōs estai to sperma sou·

paragraphs.text: And without being weakened in faith he considered his own body now as good as dead (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah`s womb;
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας,
paragraphs.translit: kai mē asthenēsas tē pistei katenoēsen to heautou sōma nenekrōmenon, hekatontaetēs pou hyparchōn, kai tēn nekrōsin tēs mētras Sarras,

paragraphs.text: yet, looking unto the promise of God, he wavered not through unbelief, but waxed strong through faith, giving glory to God,
paragraphs.original: εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ
paragraphs.translit: eis de tēn epangelian tou theou ou diekrithē tē apistia alla enedynamōthē tē pistei, dous doxan tō theō

paragraphs.text: and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was able also to perform.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai plērophorētheis hoti ho epēngeltai dynatos estin kai poiēsai.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore also it was reckoned unto him for righteousness.
paragraphs.original: διὸ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
paragraphs.translit: dio elogisthē autō eis dikaiosynēn.

paragraphs.text: Now it was not written for his sake alone, that it was reckoned unto him;
paragraphs.original: Οὐκ ἐγράφη δὲ διʼ αὐτὸν μόνον ὅτι ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ,
paragraphs.translit: Ouk egraphē de diʼ auton monon hoti elogisthē autō,

paragraphs.text: but for our sake also, unto whom it shall be reckoned, who believe on him that raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ διʼ ἡμᾶς οἷς μέλλει λογίζεσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν ἐγείραντα Ἰησοῦν τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
paragraphs.translit: alla kai diʼ hēmas hois mellei logizesthai, tois pisteuousin epi ton egeiranta Iēsoun ton kyrion hēmōn ek nekrōn,

paragraphs.text: who was delivered up for our trespasses, and was raised for our justification.
paragraphs.original: ὃς παρεδόθη διὰ τὰ παραπτώματα ἡμῶν καὶ ἠγέρθη διὰ τὴν δικαίωσιν ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hos paredothē dia ta paraptōmata hēmōn kai ēgerthē dia tēn dikaiōsin hēmōn.
